story.iWant: comprehensive ETL metrics collection with structured logging
story.soThat: I can monitor system health and diagnose issues quickly
story.tasks: - Extend ETLMetrics Pydantic model with additional fields for detailed error tracking - Implement structured logging using Python logging with JSON formatter - Create metrics storage directory structure at `data/metrics/{etl_name}/` - Update BaseETL to automatically save metrics after each run - Add error context preservation with stack traces and input data

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: - Given the existing BaseETL framework, when any ETL pipeline runs, then it automatically collects and stores: start_time, end_time, items_processed, items_failed, errors_detail, checkpoint_status - And metrics are stored in JSON format at `data/metrics/{etl_name}/{timestamp}_metrics.json` - And structured logging includes: log level, timestamp, component, operation, context data - And error context is preserved (stack traces, input data causing errors)

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Primary Success Metrics include Daily Usage & Indispensability, Extensibility Achievement, Zero Missed Opportunities, Colleague Adoption, and System Reliability with 99%+ uptime for watchers and ETL pipelines.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Megalith's architecture is built on pragmatic, boring technology that works. This is a brownfield platform with 50+ operational ETL pipelines and a sophisticated dashboard - our architectural decisions preserve this solid foundation while enabling multi-user expansion, smart notifications, and API integrations.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: Epic Goal: Essential monitoring foundation - see system health and catch issues early. Enable all future work with robust metrics collection and provide users with basic search functionality.

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: ETLMetrics Model (Enhanced) extends existing ETLMetrics Pydantic model with additional fields for comprehensive tracking including checkpoint_status, errors_detail, memory_usage_mb, and execution_environment.

artifact.reason: Existing Pydantic model for ETL metrics that needs enhancement with additional fields for detailed error tracking and checkpoint status
Base class for all ETL processes that needs to be updated to automatically save metrics after each run
Existing structured JSON formatter for logging that provides foundation for enhanced logging with context data
Main Flask server where health API endpoints will be added in future stories

ecosystem.name: python
ecosystem.packages: pydantic>=2.11.5, pandas>=2.2.3, numpy>=2.2.5, dash>=2.0.0, psutil>=6.0.0, pytest>=7.0

constraints.constraint: Preserve existing BaseETL framework with zero disruption to 50+ ETL pipelines
Metrics collection overhead must be less than 50ms per ETL execution
Use file-based JSON storage pattern consistent with existing architecture
Maintain backward compatibility with existing ETL implementations
Never fail ETL execution due to metrics collection errors

tests.standards: Testing follows pytest framework with unit tests for BaseETL metrics collection, Pydantic model validation, and structured logging. Integration tests verify end-to-end ETL execution with metrics persistence. Performance tests ensure less than 50ms overhead for metrics collection.

ideas.idea: Test: Mock ETL execution and verify metrics object contains all required fields (start_time, end_time, items_processed, items_failed, errors_detail, checkpoint_status)
Test: Run sample ETL and verify JSON file created at correct path `data/metrics/{etl_name}/{timestamp}_metrics.json` with valid schema
Test: Create log entries and verify JSON format contains all required fields (level, timestamp, component, operation, context data)
Test: Trigger ETL error and verify error_detail includes stack trace, context, and input data
Test: Benchmark ETL execution time before and after metrics collection to verify less than 50ms overhead
